coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17), after real effort: no CERN geodetic/survey publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the FASER/TI12 tunnel location was found in this session (home.cern and the INSPIRE experiment record state only the distance/direction from ATLAS IP1, not coordinates; a Nominatim/OpenStreetMap search for the tunnel name returned only generic CERN-campus results, not a point specific to this tunnel). FASER is stated to be 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point in the unused service tunnel TI12 (src:colliders-lhc-faser-inspire-experiment-record). As a placeholder, this record reuses the numeric coordinate value already sourced for site:cern-point-1-atlas (46.2355606, 6.0546968), the nearest existing sourced CERN point, since the detector is only ~480 m from that point -- well inside this record's widened precision_m. kind is kept as 'detector' (not 'campus') because the structural validator requires kind in [detector, underground_lab] for any site holding a detector placement; confidence is 'uncertain' and this note flags the value for geographic review, exactly as site:cern-point-1-atlas and site:cern-point-8-lhcb do.
coordinates.quote: 80 hectares in the Swiss communes of Meyrin and Satigny and the French communes of Prevessin-Moens and Saint-Genis-Pouilly.

name: TI12 tunnel (FASER)
notes: TI12 is a former LEP-era transfer tunnel, 480 m downstream of ATLAS interaction point 1, reused to house the FASER detector.
REVIEW REQUIRED (A17): coordinate is a reused neighbouring-point placeholder (kind: detector, confidence: uncertain); see coordinates.note.

summary.plain: An unused service tunnel at CERN, 480 metres from the ATLAS collision point, that now holds the FASER experiment, searching for rare particles thrown straight down the beamline.
summary.technical: TI12, a former LEP transfer tunnel 480 m downstream of LHC interaction point 1 along the beam collision axis; houses the FASER detector, installed during Long Shutdown 2 (2019-2021).
